memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Routine follow‑up of atrial fibrillation.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: The patient reports occasional palpitations lasting a few seconds, no chest pain or dyspnea. She feels well otherwise and continues her school bus duties.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 158 cm gives BMI 27.2 (obese). Pulse 72 bpm regular. No peripheral oedema, lungs clear, heart sounds normal.
IMPRESSION: Atrial fibrillation on warfarin 5 mg OD with subtherapeutic INR (last 1.8). Bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD for rate control. Obesity noted; advise diet and activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg OD, repeat INR in one week. Continue bisoprolol. Advise low‑salt diet, 30 min walk daily. Influenza vaccine not due (spring). Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39 °C, or blood in stools. Please repeat these red‑flag symptoms back to me.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: INR 1.8 (target 2.0‑3.0). Serum creatinine 0.92 mg/dL (0.6‑1.2). TSH 2.1 mIU/L (0.4‑4.0).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Review of anticoagulation after dose increase.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient denies new palpitations or bleeding. Reports mild fatigue but attributes to warm weather.
EXAMINATION: BP 140/86 mmHg, weight 67.5 kg, BMI 27.0 (obese). Pulse 70 bpm regular. No jaundice, abdomen soft.
IMPRESSION: INR still subtherapeutic at 2.0 (borderline). Warfarin variability likely; consider switching to a DOAC for more stable anticoagulation. Obesity persists; reinforce diet and activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Stop warfarin, start apixaban 5 mg BD. Continue bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD. Check renal function before first dose. Return if: chest pain, breathlessness, fever >39 °C, or blood in stools. Please repeat these red‑flag symptoms back to me.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Warfarin stopped
Apixaban 5 mg BD
Bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD unchanged

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum creatinine 0.90 mg/dL (0.6‑1.2). TSH 2.0 mIU/L (0.4‑4.0). Apixaban level not routinely measured.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Six‑month review; patient notes mild dyspnea on climbing stairs.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Dyspnea on exertion for past month, no chest pain, palpitations infrequent. No orthopnea or PND.
EXAMINATION: BP 136/82 mmHg, weight 68.0 kg, BMI 27.2 (obese). Pulse 74 bpm regular. Lung bases clear, no crackles. No peripheral oedema.
IMPRESSION: Atrial fibrillation on apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, rate controlled. Obesity unchanged; advise diet and activity. No signs of heart failure.
ARRANGEMENTS: Order ECG to confirm rhythm. Continue current meds. Reinforce low‑salt diet, 30 min brisk walk daily. Influenza vaccine not due (summer). Return if: chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39 °C, or blood in stools. Please repeat these red‑flag symptoms back to me.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: ECG shows normal sinus rhythm with average ventricular rate 72 bpm. No ST‑T changes. QRS duration 92 ms. No evidence of recent ischemia.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve noticed slight swelling around my ankles by the end of the day, especially after driving the bus. It’s not painful and goes down overnight. Should I be worried?

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Evaluate ankle swelling and review overall status.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports bilateral mild ankle swelling worsening after prolonged standing, resolves overnight. No dyspnea at rest, no chest pain.
EXAMINATION: BP 138/84 mmHg, weight 68.5 kg, BMI 27.3 (obese). Pulse 73 bpm regular. Mild pitting edema up to mid‑calf bilaterally, lungs clear, JVP not elevated.
IMPRESSION: Atrial fibrillation on apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD. Mild dependent edema likely venous stasis from prolonged sitting/standing; early heart failure less likely given normal lungs and JVP. Obesity persists; advise diet and activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Add furosemide 20 mg OD for edema, review in 2 weeks. Continue apixaban and bisoprolol. Administer influenza vaccine today (09/05/2025) – patient over 60 with chronic illness. Return if: sudden increase in edema, shortness of breath at rest, chest pain, fever >39 °C, or blood in stools. Please repeat these red‑flag symptoms back to me.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 15‑Nov‑2025 at 10:30 am with Dr Priya Natarajan (D03).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: Routine chronic disease review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient feels well, denies palpitations, dyspnea, or edema. Reports good adherence to meds and daily walks.
EXAMINATION: BP 134/80 mmHg, weight 67.8 kg, BMI 27.1 (obese). Pulse 70 bpm regular. No peripheral edema, lungs clear.
IMPRESSION: Atrial fibrillation on apixaban 5 mg BD, bisoprolol 2.5 mg OD, furosemide 20 mg OD as needed. Obesity unchanged; reinforce diet and activity. No signs of decompensation.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current meds. No influenza vaccine needed (outside autumn). Return if: chest pain, breathlessness at rest, fever >39 °C, or blood in stools. Please repeat these red‑flag symptoms back to me.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.8 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.9 mmol/L (<2.6 borderline), HDL 1.2 mmol/L (>1.0 good), Triglycerides 1.4 mmol/L (<1.7). Fasting blood sugar 5.6 mmol/L (<6.1 normal). Serum creatinine 0.88 mg/dL (0.6‑1.2). TSH 1.9 mIU/L (0.4‑4.0).
